them is at least six months old. These are the last figures these companies
chose to publish, which makes every one of them a floor, not a ceiling.

easiest number in this talk to misread. On the work I was already doing — the production systems, the feature

for the conversations that actually decide deals, where salespeople rehearse
the hard ones against an AI counterpart that reacts not just to what they
say, but to how they say it. And there is a discipline that comes with all this. When code is this

living in a different world.

up, the constraint moved to raw cotton. And when the cotton gin flooded the
market with cotton, the constraint snapped back to weaving, and the power loom
answered it. It never ends. It circles. Every time a bottleneck is removed, the constraint moves upstream. Not
away. Upstream. The same thing is happening in radiology right now. Geoffrey
Hinton predicted AI would replace radiologists within five years. Instead,
salaries went up 44%, and AI mammography catches 29% more cancers. When the
cost collapsed, demand exploded, and the constraint moved to the humans
interpreting the results. So the middle is compressing, and the constraint is moving to clarity,
judgment and system design. Armin Ronacher has the operating principle: figure
out your bottleneck, automate it, then find the next bottleneck. That is the
new stack.

Start with context. We always needed it. The first wave was copy-pasting code into a chat
window, and the context was never enough. You have all lived that. What
changed is that agents can now go and find the context themselves. They
navigate the project, read the files, build their own picture. But every context window is finite, and models reason worse as it
fills up. So context engineering is not dumping everything in. It is getting
the important information into that budget. Right information, right order,
